Source map

Requirements and internal guidance

Federal regulation 33 CFR 6.16-1

Immediate reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents involving a vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility.

 Federal regulation 33 CFR 101.635

Cybersecurity drills and exercises, including communication, coordination, resources, response, and active CySO participation.

 Federal regulation 33 CFR 101.650

Cybersecurity measures covering resilience, incident response, reporting, backups, segmentation, supply chain, and physical security.

 U.S. Coast Guard Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System final rule

Final rule published January 17, 2025, effective July 16, 2025.

Facilitator guide

How to run the exercise

  1. Prepare the room. Assign participant roles and brief any field mission role player before starting.
  2. Release one inject at a time. Teams discuss privately and submit one response with their assumptions.
  3. Do not coach the answer. Ask what information the team used, what remains unknown, and who owns the decision.
  4. Reveal the guide after submissions. Compare the decisions with the internal process and cited requirements.
  5. Close with corrective actions. Record owners and dates. Keep the exported record with the exercise documentation.
Compliance note

This tool supports an exercise. It does not replace the approved Facility Security Plan, Cybersecurity Plan, Cyber Incident Response Plan, or direction from the cognizant Captain of the Port.
